mods.description: Whenever you deal damage with the weapon and roll a 1 or a 2 on the damage dice, the damage is increased by 2. This modification is permanent and cannot be switched. (p. 65)

mods.name: Light Build
mods.equippable_weapons: Melee weapons
mods.description: The weapon’s AP decreases by 1 to a minimum of 3, its load decreases by half, and its Strength requirement decreases by 1. The weapon gains Breakable. This modification is permanent and cannot be switched. (p. 65)

mods.name: Sharpened, Serrated, or Barbed
mods.equippable_weapons: Melee weapons
mods.description: The weapon gains Mangle. (p. 65)

mods.name: Ergonomic
mods.equippable_weapons: Melee weapons
mods.description: The weapon’s critical chance decreases by 1. (p. 65)

mods.name: Auto-Firing Turret
mods.equippable_weapons: Any weapon.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 3. The weapon is mounted to an immovable stand that turns and aims automatically using artificial intelligence that locks onto targets. The turret must remain connected to the terminal via wiring. Before activating the turret, you can designate any number of creatures who will not be targeted by the turret. You can spend 6 AP to activate or deactivate the turret from its terminal. When you roll combat sequence, roll combat sequence for the turret. The turret’s bonus to combat sequence is equal to your Intelligence ability modifier. On each of the turrets turns it gains 10 AP which it uses to attack the closest creature in the weapon’s short range. It does not spend its AP to do anything else. The turret is considered a robot with 25 hit points and an AC of 10. If the turret falls to 0 hit points, it ceases function and the weapon gains 1 level of decay. (p. 75)

mods.name: Bayonet
mods.equippable_weapons: Any ranged weapon with the Two Handed property.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 1. Attach a knife or combat knife to the front of the weapon, you can attack with the knife without spending AP to switch weapons. (p. 75)

mods.name: Boosted Capacitor
mods.equippable_weapons: Any energy weapon. A weapon cannot have a boosted capacitor if it has an overclocked capacitor.
mods.time: 60 - (5 x your Intelligence score) in minutes.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 3. Enhanced power consumption of the primary energy chassis. When you attack with a weapon that has this modification, you can spend 2 rounds of ammunition instead of 1 to increase the damage by 2. (p. 75)

mods.name: Double Action
mods.equippable_weapons: Any revolver.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A revolver trigger mechanism upgrade fires the round and cocks the hammer simultaneously. When you spend AP to attack with the weapon, it costs 1 less to a minimum of 1. (p. 75)

mods.name: Ergonomic Grip
mods.equippable_weapons: Any weapon.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. An overall improvement to the weapon’s grip, handling, and design to allow easier and more comfortable use. The weapon’s critical hit damage modifier or damage dice increases by 1. (p. 75)

mods.name: Hardened Receiver
mods.equippable_weapons: Any handgun, submachine gun, rifle, or shotgun. A weapon cannot have a hardened receiver if it has a Light Build.
mods.time: 60 - (5 x your Intelligence score) in minutes.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 3. An improvement to the firing mechanism to increase the power of the projectile. The weapon gains Destructive and Powerful. If the weapon already has Destructive, then the weapon’s damage dice rank increases once to a maximum of d12. The weapon’s load increases by 2. (p. 75)

mods.name: Holographic weapon sight
mods.equippable_weapons: Any ranged weapon. A weapon cannot have a Holographic weapon sight if it already has a Scope or Infrared Scope.
mods.time: 5 - (your Intelligence score) in minutes. Minimum of 1 minute.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A holographic reticle that is projected onto a non-magnifying sight. The weapon’s attack roll total is increased by 1. The weapon’s load increases by 1. (p. 75)

mods.name: Improved Rifling
mods.equippable_weapons: Any handgun, submachine gun, or rifle except for the Flare Gun, H&H Tools nail gun, or Railway Rifle.
mods.time: 60 - (5 x your Intelligence score) in minutes.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. An upgrade to the grooves in the barrel of a firearm. The weapon’s range modifiers are increased by half. (p. 76)

mods.name: Increased Clip Size
mods.equippable_weapons: Any handgun, submachine gun, rifle, or shotgun that does not have Manual Reload or Quick Reload.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 1. A longer and larger clip that feeds into the magazine to allow more rounds to be fired. The weapon’s number of rounds is increased by 3. (p. 76)

mods.name: Infrared Scope
mods.equippable_weapons: Any revolver or rifle including the Laser Rifle, Plasma Rifle, or Gauss Rifle. A weapon cannot have an Infrared Scope if it already has a Scope or Holographic weapon sight.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A highly technological pre-war wonder that uses thermal imaging to locate targets. The weapon’s long range modifier is tripled. However, any attacks made at targets within 30 feet are made at disadvantage. You can target creatures that are hidden, shrouded, in complete darkness, or invisible so long as they are not behind full cover. Additionally, the weapons attack rolls are increased by 2. The weapon’s load increases by 2. (p. 76)

mods.name: Laser Sight
mods.equippable_weapons: Any handgun, rifle, or energy weapon except for the Tri-Beam Laser Rifle, Multiplas Rifle, or Gatling Laser.
mods.time: 5 - (your Intelligence score) in minutes. Minimum of 1 minute.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A device that projects a beam onto targets, providing a visual reference point. The weapon gains Accurate. If it already has Accurate, then whenever the weapon critically hits; the damage is doubled. The weapon’s load increases by 1. (p. 76)

mods.name: Light Build
mods.equippable_weapons: Any weapon. A weapon cannot have a Light Build if it is Strengthened.
mods.time: 60 - (5 x your Intelligence score) in minutes.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. Replacing parts of the weapon with lighter materials for rebalance and ease of operation. The weapon’s load decreases by half. The weapon’s Strength requirement decreases by 1. The weapon gains Breakable. (p. 76)

mods.name: Longer Barrel
mods.equippable_weapons: Any handgun, rifle, or energy weapon.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. An increase on the length of the barrel to provide more range at the cost of poorer short range. The weapon’s long range modifier increases by 10. The weapon’s short range modifier decreases by 2. The weapon’s load increases by 4. (p. 76)

mods.name: Lucky Charm
mods.equippable_weapons: Any weapon.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 1. A little attachment that personalized your weapon. The weapon’s critical hit chance decreases by 1. Each player character can only benefit from one lucky charm. (The charm can be moved to other weapons, but you cannot have two charms on two different weapons.) (p. 76)

mods.name: Muzzle Brake
mods.equippable_weapons: Any handgun, submachine gun, rifle, or shotgun except for the Flare Gun, H&H Tools nail gun, or Railway Rifle.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A device that is fitted to the muzzle of a firearm to redirect propellant gasses outwards to reduce both recoil and muzzle rise. The weapon’s attack roll total is increased by 1. The weapon’s Strength requirement decreases by 1. The weapon’s load increases by 2. (p. 76)

mods.name: On-Board Target Tracking
mods.equippable_weapons: Any energy weapon except for the Gauss rifle, Gauss pistol, or Gatling Gun.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A gyroscopic muzzle synchronized with the weapons sights and utilizing an artificial intelligence that locks onto targets and significantly improves aim. Before you make an attack with a weapon that has this modification, you can spend 6 AP to mark a target creature within the weapon’s short range. Attack rolls against the marked creature have advantage. (p. 76)

mods.name: Overclocked Capacitor
mods.equippable_weapons: Any energy weapon that doesn’t have automatic or charge. A weapon cannot have an overclocked capacitor if it has a boosted capacitor.
mods.time: 60 - (5 x your Intelligence score) in minutes.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 3. Even further improvements to the weapons power consumption. When you attack with a weapon that has this modification, you can spend 3 rounds of ammunition instead of 1 to increase the damage by 4. (p. 76)

mods.name: Remote Controlled Turret
mods.equippable_weapons: Any weapon.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 3. The weapon is mounted to an immovable stand that turns and aims based on your input from a nearby terminal. The turret must remain connected to the terminal via wiring. You can spend 6 AP to activate or deactivate the turret from its terminal. You can spend AP to attack with a weapon that you place onto the mount. The amount of AP required to attack is reduced by 2 to a minimum of 3. If your Intelligence ability score is less than the weapons Strength requirement, you have disadvantage on attack rolls while operating the weapon in this way. The turret is considered a robot with 25 hit points and an AC of 10. If the turret falls to 0 hit points, it ceases function and the weapon gains 1 level of decay. (p. 77)

mods.name: Scope
mods.equippable_weapons: Any revolver or rifle. The Laser Rifle, Plasma Rifle, or Gauss Rifle. A weapon cannot have a Scope if it already has an Infrared Scope or Holographic weapon sight.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A simple glass scope that allows for distant magnification, for weapons that already have a scope; this modification increases the magnification. The weapon’s short range modifier is doubled and the long range modifier is quadrupled. However, any attacks made at targets within 50 feet are made at disadvantage. The weapon’s load increases by 2. (p. 77)

mods.name: Semi-Automatic
mods.equippable_weapons: Any weapon that doesn’t have Manual Reload, Quick Reload, Automatic, Area of Effect, or Energy Weapon.
mods.time: 60 - (5 x your Intelligence score) in minutes.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 3. An overhaul of the weapon’s firing mechanism to allow rounds to be much more quickly loaded into its chamber. The weapon gains Semi-Automatic. (p. 77)

mods.name: Silencer
mods.equippable_weapons: Any handgun, submachine gun, rifle, or shotgun except for the Flare Gun, H&H Tools nail gun, or Railway Rifle.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. A muzzle device that reduces the acoustic intensity of the muzzle report. While you are hidden; any attack rolls you make with a weapon that has a silencer modification does not reveal your presence to nearby creatures, allowing you to remain hidden except against the creature you attacked. The weapon’s load increases by 2. The weapon’s damage dice rank decreases once to a minimum of d4. (p. 77)

mods.name: Speedloader
mods.equippable_weapons: Any revolver.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 0. A device used for loading multiple chambers of a revolver simultaneously. You can choose to reload the weapon with 4 AP. (p. 77)

mods.name: Stock
mods.equippable_weapons: Any submachine gun, rifle, shotgun, energy weapon, or revolver with the long barrel modification.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 2. Added back portion that provides structural support, for weapons that already have a stock; this modification improves them. The weapon’s attack roll total is increased by 1. The weapon’s load increases by 4. (p. 77)

mods.name: Strengthen
mods.equippable_weapons: Any weapon. A weapon cannot be Strengthened if it has a Light Build.
mods.time: 60 - (5 x your Intelligence score) in minutes.
mods.description: Mod Slot Total: 3. Reinforcing the weapon’s structure and improving its weaker mechanisms and flaws. The weapon gains Sturdy and Defensive. The weapon’s load increases by 2. (p. 77)

ammo.name: Cryo Cell
ammo.description: Energy weapons use a unique type of ammunition akin to batteries. Instead of each round being individually loaded into a magazine or chamber, energy weapons draw power from a single cell and turn it into blasts of energy. For example, a single energy cell provides 30 rounds in a laser pistol. Meaning, to fire a laser pistol 30 times, you only require 1 energy cell. Meanwhile, a 10mm pistol can fire 12 rounds; you would need to acquire all twelve individual 10mm rounds. (p. 67)

chems.name: Buffout
chems.description:
Usage. You can use a chem with 4 AP. (p. 88)

Chem Limit. Using too many chems in a short period of time can result in overdosing. Your chem limit is equal to 2 plus half of your Endurance modifier (rounded down) (minimum of 1, maximum of 4). For each Chem that you use beyond your limit within a day, you gain 5 levels of exhaustion. (p. 88)

Duration. All chem effects last for 1 hour. (p. 88)

Addiction and Side Effects. Every chem has this property. If you use a chem you must succeed an Endurance ability check equal to 6. If you fail, you become addicted to the chem. While you are addicted to the chem, and not under the chem’s effects, you gain the associated effect listed below. You lose your chem addiction if you spend a number of weeks equal to 6 minus your Endurance ability ability modifier (minimum 1). Buffout, Buffjet, and Bufftats. Disadvantage on all Strength and Endurance ability and skill checks. Calmex, Jet, Jet fuel, Rebound, Rocket, and Ultrajet. Disadvantage on all Agility ability and skill checks. Cigarette and Coyote tobacco chew. Disadvantage on all Perception ability and skill checks. Daddy-O. Your passive sense decreases by 5. Day Tripper. Your karma cap does not flip back over when you critically fail your attack roll, nor when you are hit by a critical hit. Fury, Overdrive, and all Psychos. Your AC decreases by 2. Hydra. Your maximum HP is reduced by a number equal to your level. Med-X. When you take damage to your hit points, the damage is increased by 2. All Mentats. Disadvantage on all Charisma ability and skill checks. Steady. Your attack roll totals are decreased by 2. (p. 88)

chems.name: Buffjet
chems.description:
Usage. You can use a chem with 4 AP. (p. 88)

Chem Limit. Using too many chems in a short period of time can result in overdosing. Your chem limit is equal to 2 plus half of your Endurance modifier (rounded down) (minimum of 1, maximum of 4). For each Chem that you use beyond your limit within a day, you gain 5 levels of exhaustion. (p. 88)

chems.description:
Usage. You can use a program with 4 AP. (p. 90)

RAM Limit. Using too many programs in a short period of time can result in lag and overheating when your random-access memory isn’t large enough. Your RAM limit is equal to 2 plus half of your Endurance modifier (rounded down) (minimum of 1, maximum of 4). For each program that you use beyond your limit within a day, you gain 5 levels of exhaustion. (p. 90)

Duration. All program effects last for 1 hour. (p. 90)

While your programming is faulty, and you are not under the program’s effects, you gain the associated effect listed below. medicine.name: Addictol
medicine.description: This miracle drug comes in an inhaler. You can spend 4 AP to consume it. When you do; you become cured of all addictions. However, you gain three levels of dehydration, hunger, and exhaustion. (p. 86)

medicine.name: Antibiotics
medicine.description: This bottled medicine can stop diseases. How it affects the disease you contracted is dependent on the disease. You can consume this bottled medicine with 5 AP. (p. 86)

medicine.name: Antivenom
medicine.description: You can consume this bottled medicine with 5 AP. If you do; you become resistant to poison damage dealt to your hit points for the next 6 hours. (p. 86)

medicine.name: Cateye
medicine.description: You can consume this small pill with 3 AP. If you do; you have night vision for the next 3 hours. (p. 86)

medicine.name: Doctor’s Bag
medicine.description: This bag includes specialized tools, bandages, gauze, and healing serums to provide medical aid. You can use this kit on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. When you use it, choose one of the following actions. - Tourniquet. Spend 6 AP and remove up to two levels of bleeding. - Pain Killer. Spend 6 AP to heal a dying creature 1 hit point. - Stitch Wounds. Spend 10 minutes and heal a creature with a number of hit points equal to double their healing rate + your medicine skill bonus. - Set Bone. Spend 10 minutes and a creature with the Broken Arm or Broken Leg condition may remove it. After you have used three of these actions, the doctor’ bag supplies are used and it no longer functions. (p. 86)

medicine.name: Fixer
medicine.description: A small pill typically found in a tin with up to 5. You can spend 4 AP to consume it. When you do; you become cured of one addiction of your choice. However, you gain one level of dehydration, hunger, and exhaustion. (p. 86)

medicine.name: First Aid Kit
medicine.description: You can use this kit on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. When you use it, choose one of the following actions. - Tourniquet. Spend 6 AP and remove up to two levels of bleeding. - Pain Killer. Spend 6 AP to heal a dying creature 1 hit point. - Stitch Wounds. Spend 10 minutes and heal a creature with a number of hit points equal to double their healing rate + your medicine skill bonus. After you have used one of these actions, the first aid kit’s supplies are used and it no longer functions. (p. 86)

medicine.name: Healing Powder
medicine.description: You can spend 6 AP to use this medicinal item on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. If that creature is a human, mutant, abomination, animal, or insect; at the start of each of their turns they heal a number of hit points equal to half their healing rate (rounded down). After healing for three rounds, the effects cease. Ghouls, robots, and gen-2 synths are unaffected by healing powder (p. 86)

medicine.name: RadAway
medicine.description: You can spend 15 minutes to use this medicinal item on yourself or a creature within 5 feet of you. At the end of the hour, the affected creature removes two levels of radiation but gains one level of thirst. (p. 86)

medicine.name: RadAway (Diluted)
medicine.description: You can spend 15 minutes to use this medicinal item on yourself or a creature within 5 feet of you. At the end of the hour, the affected creature removes one level of radiation but gains one level of thirst. (p. 86)

medicine.name: Rad-X
medicine.description: You can consume this small pill with 3 AP. If you do; your radiation DC decreases by 2 for the next 3 hours. You can consume a total of three Rad-X at one time to gain their benefits, if you consume more than three you do not gain any additional benefits. (p. 86)

medicine.name: RobCo Quick Fix-it 1.0
medicine.description: The RobCo Quick Fix-it 2.0 is the new and improved healing stim but for robots! You can spend 4 AP to use this item on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. If that creature is a robot or gen-2 synth; they heal a number of hit points equal to their healing rate. (p. 87)

medicine.name: RobCo Quick Fix-it 2.0
medicine.description: The RobCo Quick Fix-it 2.0 is the new and improved healing stim but for robots! You can spend 4 AP to use this item on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. If that creature is a robot or gen-2 synth; they heal a number of hit points equal to their healing rate. (p. 87)

medicine.name: Extreme Damages RobCo Quick Fix-it 2.0
medicine.description: The Extreme Damages RobCo Quick Fix-it 2.0 is a healing stim but for robots in severe cases of major damages! You can spend 4 AP to use this item on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. If that creature is a robot or gen-2 synth; they heal a number of hit points equal to double their healing rate. (p. 87)

medicine.name: Stimpak
medicine.description: You can spend 4 AP to use this medicinal item on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. If that creature is a human, mutant, abomination, animal, or insect; they heal a number of hit points equal to their healing rate. If that creature is a ghoul; they heal a number of hit points equal to half their healing rate. (p. 87)

medicine.name: Stimpak (Diluted)
medicine.description: You can spend 4 AP to use this medicinal item on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. If that creature is a human, mutant, gen-2 synth, abomination, animal, or insect; they heal a number of hit points equal to half their healing rate. If that creature is a ghoul; they heal a number of hit points equal to a quarter of their healing rate. (p. 87)

medicine.name: Super Stimpak
medicine.description: You can spend 4 AP to use this medicinal item on yourself or another creature so long as they are next to you. If that creature is a human, mutant, gen-2 synth, abomination, animal, or insect; they heal a number of hit points equal to double their healing rate. If that creature is a ghoul; they heal a number of hit points equal to their healing rate. (p. 87)

medicine.name: Auto-Inject Stimpak
medicine.description: When your hit points are equal to or lower than half their maximum (rounded down) for the first time on a turn; you automatically gain the effects of a stimpak. (p. 87)

medicine.name: Auto-Inject Super Stimpak
medicine.description: When your hit points are equal to or lower than half their maximum (rounded down) for the first time on a turn; you automatically gain the effects of a super stimpak. (p. 87)

food.name: BlamCo Mac & Cheese
food.description: Some of the most important things that almost everyone needs in the wasteland. Folks have found new ways to prepare and consume food and drinks. Pre-made food is among the large quantities of canned or otherwise preserved food that last beyond the war. Cooked food has been prepared much more recently. Some drinks have been bottled since before the war and still taste fresh. Consumption. If you’re someone who needs to consume food and drink to survive, whenever you consume any food you remove one level of hunger and whenever you consume any drink, you remove one level of dehydration. You do not gain the benefits or the effects of any foods until after 1 minute. However, you gain the benefits and effects of drinks immediately after you consume them. Spoiled. Cooked food becomes spoiled after 3 days, and any food that remains in an irradiated zone for more than an hour becomes spoiled. If you eat spoiled food, you contract dysentery. (p. 82)

Some drinks have been bottled since before the war and still taste fresh. Consumption. If you’re someone who needs to consume food and drink to survive, whenever you consume any food you remove one level of hunger and whenever you consume any drink, you remove one level of dehydration. You do not gain the benefits or the effects of any foods until after 1 minute. However, you gain the benefits and effects of drinks immediately after you consume them. Spoiled. Cooked food becomes spoiled after 3 days, and any food that remains in an irradiated zone for more than an hour becomes spoiled. If you eat spoiled food, you contract dysentery. (p. 82)

gear.name: Bag, Backpack
gear.description:
A leather, burlap, or cloth bag with straps or a sling to grant you more space to store items on you. While you wear a backpack, your carry load increases by 50. (p. 82)

There are many types of bags in the wasteland that allow you to carry items and increase your space. If you wear more than one bag that has items stored in it, you are encumbered unless your Strength or Endurance score is greater than or equal to 8. (p. 80)

gear.name: Bag, Camping Backpack
gear.description:
This large, heavy duty backpack has nylon strings made for tightening, a waist belt to help balance, many pockets, and an overhead compartment for larger storage. While you wear a camping backpack, your carry load increases by 100. (p. 82)

There are many types of bags in the wasteland that allow you to carry items and increase your space. If you wear more than one bag that has items stored in it, you are encumbered unless your Strength or Endurance score is greater than or equal to 8. (p. 80)

gear.name: Bag, Range
gear.description:
This single bag with one sling is longer to allow weapons to be stored in it with ease. You can store up to three weapons in the bag that have the Two Handed or Unwieldy property, if you do; each weapon’s carry load is halved. (p. 82)

There are many types of bags in the wasteland that allow you to carry items and increase your space. If you wear more than one bag that has items stored in it, you are encumbered unless your Strength or Endurance score is greater than or equal to 8. (p. 80)

effects.text: Bag, Range: You can store up to three weapons in the bag that have the Two Handed or Unwieldy property, if you do; each weapon’s carry load is halved.

gear.name: Bandolier
gear.description: This pocketed strap fits across any part of the body to allow for additional items to be carried. It is not considered a bag allowing you to wear it and a backpack without becoming encumbered. While you wear a bandolier your carry load increases by 25. (p. 82)

gear.name: Ball Bearings
gear.description: You can spend 3 AP to scatter these small metal spheres across a flat surface in a 5 foot radius. Any creature who walks or runs through the area falls prone and takes 1d4 impact damage, unless the creature has a passive sense above 15 or has otherwise noticed the ball bearings; they must spend 2 AP for every 5 feet of movement. (p. 82)

effects.text: Ball Bearings: You can spend 3 AP to scatter these small metal spheres across a flat surface in a 5 foot radius. …

gear.name: Bear Trap
gear.description: You can spend 6 Action Points to arm this bear trap in a 5 foot area. If the trap is already triggered, you can reset it with 6 AP and a Strength check of 15. If a creature moves into the area, the trap triggers and they take 3d4 piercing damage to their hit points and become grappled. You can disarm an untriggered bear trap with 6 AP and a crafting skill check with the DC equal to 15. You can attempt to pry open a triggered bear trap with 6 AP and a Strength ability check equal to 15. If you are grappled by the bear trap when you attempt this ability check; you have disadvantage on the roll unless your Endurance is equal to 6 or greater. On a success, you open the bear trap and any creatures grappled by it are no longer grappled. On a failure, the trap clamps back down on the grappled creature and they take 1d4 piercing damage. (p. 82)

effects.text: Bear Trap: You can spend 6 Action Points to arm this bear trap in a 5 foot area. If the trap is already triggered, you can reset it with 6 AP and a Strength check of 15. …

gear.name: Binoculars
gear.description: You can spend 3 AP to look through binoculars. While you look through them, your sight is magnified. You have advantage on any perception ability checks relying on sight when viewing objects, creatures, or a location that are at least 100 feet away. (p. 82)

effects.text: Binoculars: You can spend 3 AP to look through binoculars. While you look through them, your sight is magnified. …

gear.name: Caltrops
gear.description: You can spend 3 AP to scatter these small sharp objects across a flat surface in a 5 foot radius. Any creature who walks or runs through the area takes 2 piercing damage to their hit points for every 1 foot of movement they make through the area (this damage is not subtracted by DT), unless the creature has a passive sense above 15 or has otherwise noticed the caltrops; they must spend 2 AP for every 5 feet of movement. (p. 82)

effects.text: Caltrops: You can spend 3 AP to scatter these small sharp objects across a flat surface in a 5 foot radius. …

gear.name: Canteen
gear.description: The metal canteen holds 32 oz. of liquid. (p. 82)

effects.text: Canteen: The metal canteen holds 32 oz. of liquid.

gear.name: Chain
gear.description: Outside of the typical, practical uses of a chain; if you are holding a chain while attempting to grapple or strangle another creature, you have advantage on your Strength ability rolls. Chains have an AC of 10, a DT of 10, 10 hit points, and vulnerability to ballistic, laser, and plasma damage. (p. 82)

effects.text: Chain: Outside of the typical, practical uses of a chain; if you are holding a chain while attempting to grapple or strangle another creature, you have advantage on your Strength ability rolls. …

gear.name: Flare
gear.description: You can spend 6 AP on your turn to light this flare. This flare creates bright red light in a 30 foot radius and dim red light for an additional 30 feet. This light lasts for 1 hour. (p. 82)

effects.text: Flare: You can spend 6 AP on your turn to light this flare. This flare creates bright red light in a 30 foot radius and dim red light for an additional 30 feet. This light lasts for 1 hour.

gear.name: Flashlight
gear.description: You can spend 1 AP while holding this flashlight to create bright light in a 20 foot cone and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light lasts for 8 hours so long as you spend 6 AP to load an energy cell into the flashlight. (p. 82)

effects.text: Flashlight: You can spend 1 AP while holding this flashlight to create bright light in a 20 foot cone and dim light for an additional 20 feet. …

gear.name: Gas mask
gear.description: While you wear this mask, your radiation DC decreases by 3 and your passive sense decreases by 2. (p. 82)

gear.name: Geiger Counter
gear.description: When you enter an irradiated zone, this device detects the level of radiation and you learn the radiation severity score. (p. 82)

gear.name: Grappling Hook
gear.description: A metal hook that can be tied and attached to rope with 6 AP. (p. 82)

effects.text: Grappling Hook: A metal hook that can be tied and attached to rope with 6 AP.

gear.name: Hazmat Suit
gear.description: This large yellow suit is lined with layers of lead to provide the most protection from radiation without wearing power armor. Due to its bulky design; it takes 1 minute to don or doff, and you cannot wear armor over the suit. However, you can wear armor underneath the suit. While you wear the hazmat suit your radiation DC decreases by 10 and you are immune to radiation damage. If you fail a radiation check, your radiation DC does not increase. For every 5 points of damage you take to your hit points while wearing a hazmat suit, it gains a level of decay. Each level of decay increases your radiation score by 1. To repair a hazmat suit, the crafting DC is equal to 12 (+2) and requires x2 lead and x1 cloth. (p. 82)

effects.text: Radiation damage
Hazmat Suit: if you fail a radiation check, your radiation DC does not increase.

gear.name: Hazmat Suit, Powered
gear.description: This suit includes a geiger counter, an air purification system, impact absorption, further padding, and is topped with a bulbous helmet resembling a space suit. The suit requires power in order to operate. You can spend 6 AP to load 3 energy cells into the suit which allows it to be powered for up to 6 hours. Thanks to its automatic shrink fitting system; It takes 30 seconds to don or doff, however you cannot wear armor while wearing this suit. While you wear the hazmat suit your DT is increased by 3, you cannot gain levels of radiation, and you are immune to radiation damage. For every 5 points of damage you take to your hit points while wearing a hazmat suit, it gains a level of decay. If the suit gains 10 levels of decay, it ceases function until repaired. To repair a hazmat suit, the crafting DC is equal to 15 (+5) and requires x3 lead, x2 leather, and x2 circuitry. (p. 82)

effects.text: Radiation damage; you cannot gain levels of radiation (while powered)

gear.name: Insulated Clothing
gear.description: Heat trapping clothing, furs, weighted jackets, boots, hats, gloves, all the works to keep you warm. It takes 1 minute to put on insulated clothing and 1 minute to take it off. You are considered insulated while you wear this clothing. You cannot wear armor over this clothing (however, there is an insulated armor upgrade). While you wear insulated clothing, your maximum AP is reduced by 1 to a minimum of 6. (p. 82)

effects.text: Insulated (hypothermia)

gear.name: Insulated Clothing, Lightweight
gear.description: The wonders of prewar thermal ingenuity. This trendy set of nylon, fabric, and heat trapping cotton can keep you warm without all the bulk. This clothing’s properties are identical to the normal insulated clothing, however your AP is not reduced. (p. 82)

effects.text: Insulated (hypothermia)

gear.name: Lockpicks
gear.description: These metal tools allow you to pick locks with far more proficiency. When you make a breach skill check to pick a lock, the DC is reduced by 5. After you use these lockpicks a total of five times, they break and cease function. (p. 82)

effects.text: Lockpicks: When you make a breach skill check to pick a lock, the DC is reduced by 5. After you use these lockpicks a total of five times, they break and cease function.

gear.description: Rope can be used to tie items together, make a pulley system, climb, or tie someone up. If you are holding a rope while attempting to grapple or strangle another creature, you have advantage on your Strength ability rolls. Rope has an AC of 10, a DT of 2, 5 hit points, and vulnerability to ballistic, laser, plasma, and slashing damage. (p. 82)

effects.text: Rope: If you are holding a rope while attempting to grapple or strangle another creature, you have advantage on your Strength ability rolls. …

gear.description: This leather pouch is fitted with a cap and nozzle and holds 60 oz. of liquid. (p. 82)

gear.name: Weapon Repair Kit
gear.description: This plastic box filled with tools and mechanisms was used during the great war to repair soldiers’ weapons with ease. Though, the tech used to create them has long since been forgotten; many are still found across the wasteland. You can spend 6 AP to insert any weapon into the repair kit. After 1 minute, the weapon is ejected and loses 2 levels of decay. The weapon repair kit ceases function after it has been used a total of three times. (p. 82)

magazines.name: Milsurp Review
magazines.effect: Your Guns skill bonus increases by 1 until you rest.
magazines.description: Reading a skill magazine can give you some tips and grant an edge on your skill rolls. Skill magazines are typically found or bought in issues and they take a number of minutes to read equal to 5 minus your Intelligence ability modifier, if this number is reduced to 0 you can read the skill magazine with 6 AP. Once you read an issue of a skill magazine you can no longer gain its benefits. Be sure to keep track of which issues you’ve read after reading them. (Example: ¡La Fantoma! issue #4 read.) After you read five different issues of the same magazine, your associated skill bonus permanently increases by 1. Each magazine typically costs around 50 caps and has a load of 2 (GM’s discretion). (p. 88)

Skill magazines are typically found or bought in issues and they take a number of minutes to read equal to 5 minus your Intelligence ability modifier, if this number is reduced to 0 you can read the skill magazine with 6 AP. Once you read an issue of a skill magazine you can no longer gain its benefits. Be sure to keep track of which issues you’ve read after reading them. (Example: ¡La Fantoma! issue #4 read.) After you read five different issues of the same magazine, your associated skill bonus permanently increases by 1. Each magazine typically costs around 50 caps and has a load of 2 (GM’s discretion). (p. 88)

unique_items.description:
A RobCo Stealth Boy 3001 personal stealth device. This technological, pre-war wonder generates a modulating field that transmits the reflected light from one side of an object to the other. You can spend 3 AP to activate a stealth boy, once you activate you become invisible for 1 minute so long as you keep the stealth boy on your body. unique_items.name: Two-way Radio
unique_items.description:
These small militaristic devices allow for long range communication. The dual radios function so long as you spend 6 AP to load an energy cell into each one, in which they each last for a total of 100 activations. You can spend 3 AP to activate one of the radios, when you activate it; any sound made within 5 feet of the radio is transmitted to the other radio which can be heard out to a range of 5 feet. If both radios are activated simultaneously, neither emit any sound. (p. 91)

currency.name: Caps
currency.description: Bottle caps, the currency of the wasteland. (p. 55)

steps.title: Race variant
steps.description: Robots must choose their type: Handy, Protectron or Robobrain. (p. 9) The other races can, if your GM allows it, start with the variant abilities (p. 7–12). Humans can take Variant Human, Gen 3 Synth, both or neither.

steps.title: S.P.E.C.I.A.L.
steps.description:
Step 2: each ability score starts at 5. At 1st level you gain 3 points which you can use to increase any ability score equal to the points used. You can also decrease any ability score to gain extra points equal to the amount decreased. Minimum 1, maximum 10. (p. 4, 19)
The text says the modifier "is equal to 5 minus your score" (p. 4), but its example and the table (p. 19) use score minus 5. The sheet follows the table.

steps.title: Negative Luck
steps.description: Your Luck modifier is negative, and the book has two rules for it (p. 4 and p. 25). Read both and pick one with your GM. You can change it later in the Character tab.

steps.title: Background
steps.description: Step 4: choose your Background. You gain a +2 to three different skills listed in your chosen Background (p. 4), its trait and its starting equipment.

steps.title: Background skills
steps.description: Custom Background: choose the three skills that get +2. (p. 13) The other backgrounds already add their +2.

steps.title: Background trait
steps.description: Custom Background: choose the trait your background gives, any trait from the list. (p. 13)

steps.title: Recluse: +2 to five skills
steps.description: Recluse: instead of gaining a perk at 1st level, five different Skill modifiers of your choice increase by 2. (p. 29)

steps.title: Talented: −2 to five skills
steps.description: Talented: you gain an extra perk at 1st level. However, five different skill modifiers of your choice decrease by 2. (p. 29)

steps.title: Trait
steps.description: Step 7: you can optionally choose a second trait besides your background’s, and optionally modify it with Wild Wasteland (the "Wild Wasteland" versions). (p. 4, 26) Traits come before perks because some change how many perks you get.

steps.title: Perk
steps.description: Step 23: choose a Perk that you meet the requirements for. (p. 4)

steps.title: Protectron: built-in tool
steps.description: Protect and Serve: choose one tool or weapon built into one of your arms. (p. 10)

steps.title: Handy: first arm
steps.description: Incredible Multi-Talented Appliance: Handys are built with three special tools, one in each of three arms. Choose the tool or weapon for your first arm. (p. 9)

steps.title: Handy: second arm
steps.description: The book says Handys are built with three tools (and can have three Grippers), but then says "choose one tool or weapon". Choose a tool for your second arm, or none, as agreed with your GM. The same tool can be chosen again. (p. 9)

steps.title: Handy: third arm
steps.description: Same as the second arm: choose a tool for your third arm, or none, as agreed with your GM. (p. 9)

steps.title: Equipment
steps.description: Step 16: add any equipment you gained from your background (the version for your race), with its decay and armor already worn. Alternatively, you can choose to take no equipment and gain 850 caps. (p. 4) What is not an item of the game goes to "Other items".

items.title: Story and appearance
items.placeholder: Where you come from, what you look like, what you seek in the wasteland…

resources.name: Group Sneak
resources.description: The average Sneak bonus of the characters (rounded down). Used while traveling at half pace.

resources.name: Party Nerve
resources.description: Charisma modifiers added together, then halved (rounded down). Added to Death Saves, and gained as temporary SP when rolling combat sequence.
